results.title: J.P.McGowan
results.creator_credit: Julie Marlow, Scott Murray and Paul Kallina
results.brief_description: Born in Terowrie, South Australia, J.P.McGowan acted in more than 270 films, many of which he directed, including the acclaimed serial The Hazards of Helen. The first Australian actor and director to ever break in to Hollywood, his film work is regarded as some of the most skilful of the period, and exists in the hands of several dedicated collectors across the globe. A pioneer Australian film maker, McGowan has left an important international legacy. This half hour film documenting the Terowrie celebration of his life, and illustrating the little known life and career of J.P.McGowan is a marvellous addition to Australian film culture. There is a large extant collection of McGowan’s work, clips from which will be sourced for inclusion in the film. The filmmakers will be in touch with the major collectorof McGowan’s work in Adelaide; and there may be an opportunity to acquire the best of it for ACMI collections

results.title: Ivan the Terrible [study extract]
results.brief_description: One of a series of short extracts from feature films intended for study of cinema technique. Ivan is portrayed as a cruel tyrant, a product of Renaissance times in “an epoch fraught with passion and blood”, struggling to unify Russia. In this excerpt Ivan is crowned Tsar of Russia in the Cathedral. Courtiers and Ambassadors discuss his popularity; there are factions for and against him. Nothing mars the ceremony, however, as the bass singer intones a liturgy, and Ivan is ceremonially showered with coins.

results.title: Ivan the Terrible [Part 1]
results.creator_credit: Mosfilm, Central Cinema Studios and Sergei Eisenstein
results.brief_description: Ivan the Terrible part one is Eisenstein’s boldest and most successful experiment in stylisation. It draws upon the other arts - Wagnerian opera, Marinsky ballet and Japanese Kabuki theatre. Ivan’s personal life is interwoven with the themes of his drive for empire and his alliance with the merchant class against the aristocracy. This is the first part of a trilogy; the second part is dominated by cloak and dagger intrigue; the final part, which was to be in colour, was designed but not filmed. Cinematography by Edouard Tisse and Andrei Moskvin. Music by Sergei Prokofieff. Cast includes Nikolai Cherkasov, Ludmilla Tselikovskaya, Seraphina Birman, Pyotr Kadochnikov. In russian with English subtitles.

results.title: Its water cycle
results.brief_description:
Episode of Series “The Earth”.
Shows clouds massing and evaporating, ice crystals growing under photomicrography, and air and water under varying pressures in a plastic box, in order to illustrate the hydrologic or evaporation-condensation-precipitation cycle.

results.title: Its oceans
results.brief_description:
Episode of Series “The Earth”.
A comprehensive study, revealing the changing pattern of the ocean’s surface, the living and non-living things in the waters, the nature of the ocean floor, and the influence of the oceans on man. The roles of modern scientists - oceanographers, marine biologists and others - as they work to gain more knowledge of the earth’s vast, deep oceans.
